html:
The Schitsu'umsh, known in English as the Coeur d'Alene, are an Interior Salish people of northern Idaho and eastern Washington, around Coeur d'Alene Lake. French fur traders called them Coeur d'Alène, "heart of an awl", said to mean that they were sharp traders.

They fished, hunted deer and dug camas roots, and after horses reached the region in the 1700s they crossed the Rockies to hunt bison. Jesuit missionaries built the Cataldo Mission among them in the 1850s; it is now the oldest standing building in Idaho. In 1858 they joined the Spokane and others in the Coeur d'Alene War against the US Army and were defeated.

Their reservation, set up in 1873, was later cut down. In 2001 the US Supreme Court confirmed that the tribe owns the southern part of the lake bed. See also Salish and Kootenai.
